passage.title: Teacher-written article extract for the Year 9 assessment point 2 test (TGA)
paras: For ninety years the ferry has crossed the sound at seven every morning. This winter it will cross for the last time. The company says a bridge is cheaper, and the company is probably right. But nobody ever made a friend on a bridge. On the ferry, the same faces meet every day: the fisherman with his flask, the nurse finishing her night shift, the boy who reads the same comic until it falls apart. Twenty minutes of grey water, and somehow a whole island learns each other's news. When the bridge opens, we will arrive faster. I am not sure we will arrive together.

questions.q: Before the timer: underline the key word in question 3

Core (timed, 20 minutes): Section A. 1) How long has the ferry run? (1) 2) Give two people the writer describes on the ferry. (2) 3) What does 'somehow' suggest about the island's news? (2) 4) How does the writer present the ferry as more than transport? Use PETZAAL. (8) 5) How does the writer structure the ending for effect? (3)
questions.a: 1) ninety years. 2) any two: the fisherman, the nurse, the boy with the comic. 3) the sharing happens naturally, almost mysteriously, without planning. 4) e.g. the list of regulars, 'nobody ever made a friend on a bridge', contrast of 'faster' and 'together'. 5) shifts from fact to personal doubt; the final short sentence balances 'faster' against 'together' to leave the reader uneasy.

questions.q: Extend (timed, 5 minutes): Section B. 6) Combine with 'whereas': 'A bridge is faster. A ferry is sociable.' (2) 7) Begin a sentence about the ferry with a subordinate clause. (2) 8) Correct: 'the islands ferry is old, it is still loved' (2)
questions.a: 6) A bridge is faster, whereas a ferry is sociable. 7) e.g. 'Although the ferry is slow, the islanders love it.' 8) The island's ferry is old, but it is still loved.

questions.q: Stretch (timed, 8 minutes): Section C. Write one paragraph arguing for or against replacing something old and loved with something new and efficient.
questions.a: Marked for a clear viewpoint, a counter-argument and persuasive methods (4) and accuracy (4).

questions.q: Question 5 asks how the writer structures the ending. What should you discuss?
options: the shift from facts to a personal, uncertain judgement in the final sentences
questions.a: A) the shift from facts to a personal, uncertain judgement in the final sentences. Structure questions are about how the text moves and ends.
